steps.text: Bring water and both sugars to a boil in a saucepan over medium heat. Reduce the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until both sugars are dissolved. Remove from the heat and let cool for 10 minutes.
Stir in vodka, almond extract, and vanilla. Store in a sealed bottle.

raw_recipe.headline: Amaretto
raw_recipe.description: This amaretto recipe lets you make this sweet liqueur at home with vodka, vanilla, almond extract, and sugar. It tastes exactly like the real thing!
raw_recipe.name: Amaretto

recipeInstructions.text: Bring water and both sugars to a boil in a saucepan over medium heat. Reduce the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until both sugars are dissolved. Remove from the heat and let cool for 10 minutes.
Stir in vodka, almond extract, and vanilla. Store in a sealed bottle.

review.reviewBody: I like Amaretto, but am a bit of a snob when it comes to the brand, I don't think anything is worth drinking unless it is the Disaronno, and I can honestly say, this recipe is so very close to Disaronno that I will make this rather than spend on the real thing now. Thank you so much for this great recipe.

I figured the best way to compare is to do a side by side comparison :) I followed the recipe exactly and used dark brown sugar. Two shots side by side the color was slightly different but I'm thinking it's just my brand of dark brown sugar. The scent of both was pretty dead on but Disarono has a slight rubbing alchohol leftover scent towards the end. Finally the taste test, the Disaronno had a slightly stronger and sharper aftertaste. This amaretto had a smoother, fuller, and a tad bit sweeter taste to it. Surprisingly I'd have to say I like this amaretto more than Disaronno. Give it a try. It's worth the effort and ingredients.

I have made this for 4 years now...it's a hit every time! 
Hints: One 1.75ml jug of vodka is almost 7.5cups. If you change the servings to 45, it will adjust everything accordingly. This works great for a large batch.
Also, seal in airtight glass bottles (washed free of any previous smells/flavors) for best results. 
This can be consumed immediately, but tastes better and better as it sits undisturbed.

I've made many batches over the past two years and this is an excellent recipe!! My only regret is not having found it before all the money I spent on Disaronno! I drink it with diet cream soda to "help" cut the calories.( I can't afford sugar substitutes) I make this recipe x 4 and store it in my frig in mason jars. I have a pour spout that fits them which makes it easy to pour. The almond extract cost was high, I now order 32 oz bottles from Amazon, as well as 11 oz bottles of vanilla. To make my quadrupled batch that is one 750 ml bottle of vodka plus one cup and everything else X 4. I also cool quickly by running cold water several times in the sink or an ice bath surrounding pan to cool quickly before adding the alcohol. Enjoy!!

Oh, Yumm! Made dark brown sugar by adding some molasses to light brown sugar. Quick cooled the pan by rubbing ice cubes over it, then took it to the neighbors for a taste test. Now I have to make her some for the W/E. This is a great recipe & so easy! Thanks for sharing, Marjory.

Better than the "real" thing! I have made this many times, and given it away as gifts. Friends are always happily anticipating the holidays, claiming this amaretto is smoother than the top brands! I double the recipe and make this in an 8 cup glass pyrex pitcher with a pour spout, in the microwave. I heat the water in the microwave, wisk in the sugars, let cool. Add cold vodka and extracts. Pour into bottles using a funnel. Definitely use dark brown sugar. Also, much better when served chilled.

Oh YES! We love Disarrono, but it just costs too much now that we are on retirement funds. So I made this today. Gave my hubby 2 glasses and asked which one he liked best. He chose THIS one! That's how good this is! 
Will be making lots more and never have to spend that good money on good booze! 
I used just 1 cup of vodka - I used a mid priced one, and doubled everything else. Also let the sugar water mixture cook for about 5 minutes after boiling, as per others suggestions. It is a little darker than the "real stuff", but not put off by that at all. Really Really Good!

Really tasty! Following other suggestions: (1) I simmered the sugar & water for a few minutes to thicken it up; (2) since many reviewers suggested dark brown sugar, but I only had light, I replaced ALL the sugar (brown and white) with light brown sugar; (3) added alcohol to taste - for sipping by itself, I used about 2/3 of the vodka called for

I doubled the sugar, tripled the vodka, doubled the vanilla and left the almond extract as is. 

Let it sit for 24 hours. 

I used premium vodka. 

My partner is not fond of the almond flavoring but likes my homemade liqueurs so I made this work. 

I let it sit in a jug and ready to pour in a glass, full of ice. 

Very fantastic!

Very good recipe for amaretto. I used dark brown sugar instead of light brown and used vanilla beans instead of vanilla extract and I let it sit overnight before bottling it and it's pretty close to tasting like Disarrono

I am really impressed with this recipe! I swapped the amounts for white and brown sugar around so my spirit is the same colour as "the original one". I also added some glycerine to get that sirope liqueur texture, don't add to much! Start with just a little and taste. Taste is really good and will improve over the weeks! Here in New Zealand you allowed to distill your own alcohol! So great to make my own almond liqueur now Thanks for sharing UPDATE 26-07-14 after a few tests I noticed that alcohol% is to low compare with the 28% amaretto from italy so I replaced the 1 cup water with alcohol (vodka) as well so three cups alcohol, no water. I don't heat it! I put everything in my Kitchen Aid machine and mix it cold for about 30 minute's so sugar is dissolved as well ( longer if needed) The alcohol I use is homebrew 40% alcohol but with all the sugar and extract you around 29% I guess. You always can the one cup water replaced with half water half alcohol if its to strong for you. Not for us living in New Zealand :-) enjoy but drink responsibly!!
I’ve made this amaretto as Christmas gifts for decades. I stock up on pretty bottles from DollarTree, and some recipients return their empty bottles for refills!
Perfect the way it is. Great over crushed ice
Made a batch a couple years ago. It is very good, especially in my Panna Cotta all'Amaretto!

This recipe is so good! I like Disaronno, but I think this is so much better. I usually follow the recipe, but I will try using some dark brown sugar next time after seeing other comments. I love to sip on this warm, it is like a hot toddy but better. I share this recipe all of the time because everyone loves it! I usually make one batch per the recipe and another batch with Fireball for an extra kick. They are both delicious!

No changes, but I swap the ratio of brown sugar to white sugar. Made this recipe many times. Making it now and wanted to thank Marjory! Indistinguishable from the original at far less cost (I use Costco vodka).

I use 190 proof Everclear- so you have to calculate the difference in volume. It works out to be 3.5 cups of everclear, and 8.5 cups of water, and then follow the recipe accordingly. One thing I also do, for extra depth and kick, I’ll add 2 cups of spiced rum, Kraken 100proof is what I use. Since that’s so flavorful already, it doesn’t dilute the flavor on its own. Thats a total of 14 cups of volume and about 34% ABV.
Delicious right from the pot. We did a taste test with one airrated (with the wine airrater) and one poured directly into the bottle. We slightly preferred the airrated one.
My family won’t drink anything else including disarrano! Been making this for years now!

I was pleasantly surprised how delicious this was and so easy to make! I have since tried to make a “healthier” alcoholic drink 😂 by cutting down the sugar - I cut out all the white sugar and it’s still delicious!
